pass_a_gloss:
saying through the lyre of the psalmist thus: I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world. He spoke also to the Jews in parables. Therefore, they did not counsel the people, but neither did the deep-voiced one know. They did not counsel so that the foolish people would not hear. For if they had counseled, the foolish people would not have heard. Blessed are those who have recognized the Redeemer. But there was no understanding for the one hearing. For the Jews, being foolish, did not discern the voices of their leaders, nor did they distinguish whether they were counseling good or doing the opposite. Behold, Zion, the city, our Savior, your eyes will see Jerusalem, a wealthy city, tents that will not be shaken, the ropes of its tent will not be broken, for the name of the Lord is great for you. A place will be yours, broad and spacious rivers and canals, and the face of the lovers of truth, who have recognized the epiphany of Christ, will be brought forth again, saying: either the Church on earth or the one in heaven, the heavenly city, the nourishment of the saints.

Therefore, since they have known Zion, in which our salvation, that is, Christ, is, and they show it to others, the divine word immediately takes over their voices and says: Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city; and it is discussed as being similar to the ancient tabernacle in the wilderness; the word calls Zion rich and the tabernacle unshakable; for it has unbroken ropes and continuously fixed pegs; the Church has been established and has a firm foundation for being well; for the gates of Hades will not prevail against it; and it gives the reason why this will be, saying to those who believe in Christ that the name of the Lord is great for them; for those who have not approached faith, the name of Christ is not great and glorified; but for us who believe, it is great and lofty; we worship Him as God, as the true Son of the Father, as the Word who became human for the salvation of all; this, it says, is the tabernacle that always remains, a place…
pass_b_english: The psalmist sings through his lyre, saying that he will open his mouth in parables and utter things hidden since the foundation of the world (Matthew 13:35).
He spoke to the Jews in parables.
Therefore, they did not counsel the people, but neither did the deep-voiced one know.
They did not counsel so that the foolish people would not hear.
For if they had counseled, the foolish people would not have heard.
Blessed are those who have recognized the Redeemer.
But there was no understanding for the one hearing.
For the Jews, being foolish, did not discern the voices of their leaders, nor did they distinguish whether they were counseling good or doing the opposite.

Behold, Zion, the city, our Savior, your eyes will see Jerusalem, a wealthy city, tents that will not be shaken, the ropes of its tent will not be broken, for the name of the Lord is great for you (Isaiah 33:20).
A place will be given to you, with broad and spacious rivers and canals.

The face of the lovers of truth, who have recognized the epiphany of Christ, will be brought forth again, saying: whether one speaks of the Church on earth or the one in heaven, the heavenly city, the nourishment of the saints, it is the same, so that even if one calls it the Church on earth or the one in heaven, the meaning is the same.
The divine word takes over the voices of those who, filled with great joy, leap for joy as they have recognized Zion, the place where our salvation, Christ, is found.
They show Zion to others, and the word says that their eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city, similar to the ancient tabernacle in the wilderness.
The Church has been established and has a firm foundation for being well, for it has unbroken ropes and continuously fixed pegs, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it (Matthew 16:18).
The reason for this is that the name of the Lord is great for those who believe in Christ.
We worship Him as God, as the true Son of the Father, as the Word who became human for the salvation of all.
This, the word says, is the tabernacle that always remains, a place…
